newsitem.title: USA: CSCE says to adjust coffee, cocoa futures margins.
newsitem.headline: CSCE says to adjust coffee, cocoa futures margins.

text.p: The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange Inc (CSCE) said Tuesday it will cut the minimum margin on spot coffee "C" contracts for exchange members and members of the trade to $2,000 from $3,000, effective Thursday.
The CSCE also announced Tuesday it would cut the minimum margin on all cocoa contract months to $400 from $500, beginning Wednesday, September 18, for exchange members and members of the trade.
Exchange officials said that due to recent declines in market volatility, higher rates were no longer justified.
"The original margins are constantly monitored and periodically changed due to market conditions, such as volatility," an exchange spokeswoman said.

For coffee futures, once the September contract expires on Wednesday, the $1,000 additional spot charge add-on will not be applied to December when it becomes the spot contract the following day, the CSCE said.
The $2,000 minimum margin will also apply to March 1997 coffee futures, the CSCE said.
Information on when the supplemental margin had been applied to the spot month on coffee was not immediately available, the CSCE said.
Margins for customers who are not members of the exchange or the trade will be a minimum of 140 percent of the above prescribed amounts for both coffee and cocoa futures, the CSCE said.

Additionally, CSCE said that after the September 1996 coffee contract expires on Wednesday, it will remove the $1,000 add-on for all straddle and arbitrage transactions involving the nearby month, lowering the margin to $700 from the current $1,700.
-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk, 212 859 1640
